newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai govt to buy more rubber from local market.
newsitem.headline: Thai govt to buy more rubber from local market.

text.p: The Thai government will buy more rubber from the local market to prop up prices after having bought around 45,000 tonnes since March, a senior agricultural ministry official told Reuters on Wednesday.

Sanit Samosorn, deputy director-general of Department of Agriculture, said the government would intervene until prices improved. But he would state what the desirable price level would be for the govenrment.
The government earlier this week bought 3,500 tonnes of RSS3 grade rubber and is negotiating to buy 2,000 tonnes of RSS4 grade.
However, trade sources said the government was now running out of space to store the rubber purchased so far and was unable to take some deliveries.
Sanit said the problem was being adressed.
"Although our warehouses are limited, we will rent more space from the private sector," he said.

In southern Trang province, some 1,000 rubber tappers have protested and blocked the street in their town since Wednesday morning and demanded that the government buy rubber from them at 30-35 baht per kg ($1.15) against the current guaranteed price of 27.5 baht.
